articles.title: India bonds wobble as supply, RBI cash-drain risks loom
articles.content: On Thursday, investor appetite for Indian government bonds dwindled amidst fears of increased supply and concerns over RBI's liquidity stance. The results from the treasury bill auction reflected weak demand, driving yields upward. Speculation is building that the Reserve Bank of India may take steps to curtail excess liquidity, preparing for possible policy adjustments as inflationary pressures rise. Market analysts predict interest rate hikes within the next year.

articles.title: Jackson Hole 2026: What to expect from Fed chair Kevin Warsh as markets stay on edge
articles.content: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s first Jackson Hole speech comes as markets grapple with sticky inflation, elevated oil prices and shifting rate expectations. Investors will watch for clues on the Fed’s policy path, while the dollar, Treasury yields and gold could react sharply to any change in Warsh’s tone.

articles.title: Sebi proposes scrapping merchant banker requirement rule for small-ticket debt via private placement
articles.content: Sebi has put forth a proposal to exempt small-value debt issuances from the requirement of appointing merchant bankers. This initiative is designed to lower compliance costs and foster market growth for listed companies. To qualify, issuers must be regulated and have been listed for a minimum of one year, along with providing an auditor’s certificate to confirm no recent defaults.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Alfred Winslow Jones: "The tools that get investors and speculators in and out of the market only after some widely followed average has turned must obviously exaggerate the movements of the market"

articles.title: Billionaire Agarwal’s Vedanta plans third rupee bond this year
articles.content: Vedanta plans to raise at least Rs 1,000 crore through rupee bonds with maturities of three to seven years, mainly to refinance debt. It would be the group’s third domestic bond issue this year. The planned borrowing comes as Indian companies increasingly tap bond markets amid expectations of possible interest-rate hikes later this year.

articles.title: Markets push back BoE rate hike expectations to February 2027
articles.content: As bond yields fall, markets are revising their expectations for the Bank of England's rate hikes. Investors now foresee a modest quarter-point increase by February 2027, with less than four basis points anticipated for the upcoming September meeting. The persistent inflation coupled with a weakening labor market is adding complexity to the monetary policy landscape, keeping a keen eye on economic indicators and central bank cues for future actions.

articles.title: Rupee dips, reversing intraday gains, as importer dollar demand dominates
articles.content: The Indian rupee declined on Thursday, reversing early gains against the dollar. Importer dollar demand increased, and month-end pressures also contributed to the fall. A modest recovery in the dollar index further dampened the rupee's momentum. Banks absorbed two days of inflows after a holiday, increasing swap costs. The rupee had previously seen its biggest single-day rise after oil prices slipped.

articles.title: Global Market: European shares steady as Nvidia boost offsets consumer, auto weakness

articles.title: Global Market: Japanese bond yields retreat after BOJ deputy governor signals no clear rate-hike timing
articles.content: Japanese government bond yields retreated from session highs after BOJ Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino offered no clear signal on the timing of the next rate hike. The two-year JGB yield briefly hit 1.70%, its highest since 1995, before easing. Investors now await Governor Kazuo Ueda’s comments for clues on the central bank’s rate-hike path and monetary policy outlook.
